To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of substance P on neuronal nicotinic receptor currents are not mediated by protein kinase c (PKC) or by guanine nucleotide-binding proteins and that the effects of OAG on these currents are not mediated through PKC.

substance P enhances the decay of the whole cell nicotine-induced current in PC-12, that this effect is not antagonized by a G protein blocker or staurosporin, a nonselectve PKC blocker, and that staurosporine fails to reverse OAG-induced inhibition of nicotine-induced current.

the effect of substance P on neuronal nAChR is not mediated by PKC or G protein and that the effect of diacylglycerols is not mediated by activation of PKC but is most likely due to a direct interaction with the receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of neuronal nicotic acetylcholine receptor (AChR) activity by substance P and diacylglycerols.
the mechanisms by which the peptide substance P modulates nicotinic acethylcholine receptors in PC12 cells.
the modulation of the neuronal nicotinic receptor (nAChR) by substance P and the mechanism of this action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
substance P is a direct modulator of nAChRs in PC-12 and other cells.
substance P and OAM modulate neuronal nAChR independently from activation of G proteins, PKC or cAMP, and that the effect of OAG is not mediated by PKC.
the effects of substance P and OAM are mediated by direct interaction with nAChRs, but that PKC does participate in the modulation by OAG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
substance P and OGA act directly on the nAChRs and that PKC activation is not involved.
the modulation by substance P of the neuronal nAChR is direct and that the modulation by OAG is indirect, involving activation of a protein kinase other than PKC.
the modulation of nAChR by substance P and DAG is a direct effect on the receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
modulation of neuronal nAChR function by substance P is a direct effect of the peptide on receptor function.
substance P modulate neuronal nAChR independently from the activation of PKC and G proteins.
substance P modulated neuronal nAChR activity by direct interaction with the receptor and independently from activation of protein kinase C or G proteins.
